detail.longDescription: I'm trying to automate taking cropped screenshots of Windows 11 UI steps (context menus, Run dialog, Registry Editor, Task Manager) using Python ( pywinauto with backend="uia" , pyautogui , and mss ). The script works fine on classic Win32 dialogs, but it breaks constantly on Windows 11's newer XAML / WinUI 3 surfaces: On the new right-click context menu ( PopupHost ), Desktop(backend="uia") either times out traversing the tree or returns stale coordinates, and the menu immediately closes if anything steals focus. Using pygetwindow.getActiveWindow() + mss often captures the underlying Explorer window instead of the popup menu or modal dialog. As a workaround I tried overlaying a 200px coordinate grid on full-screen captures and using visual detection/OCR instead of UIA, which works around the tree hangs, but still feels fragile for small menu items. Here is the simplified capture + UIA lookup I started with: import time import pyautogui from pywinauto import Desktop pyautogui.rightClick(500, 300) time.sleep(0.5) desktop = Desktop(backend="uia") # Often hangs or misses "Show more options" inside Win11 XAML context menu popup = desktop.window(class_name="PopupHost") item = popup.child_window(title="Show more options", control_type="MenuItem") rect = item.rectangle() Is there a reliable way in Python to query bounding boxes of Windows 11 XAML popups (like PopupHost ) without hanging UIA or dismissing the menu? Or is calling the Windows UI Automation COM API directly (e.g., via comtypes / uiautomation ) significantly more stable than pywinauto for WinUI 3?
